content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are small sections of a bird's wing, commonly served in fast‑food and restaurant menus. They can be baked in the oven or broiled on a grill, producing a crispy exterior and juicy meat. Often accompanied by sauces such as barbecue, ranch, or hot sauce.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are a classic appetizer in the United States and have become popular worldwide.
The traditional American "Buffalo wings" are deep‑fried, but baked versions are gaining popularity as a healthier alternative.
Wings can be coated with a variety of marinades: honey‑soy, garlic, spicy chili, and more.
In Japan, "tebasaki" are wings marinated in soy sauce and honey, then baked to a caramelized finish.
Chicken wing eating contests are common, with records measured by the number of wings consumed in a set time.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken wings provide high‑quality animal protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: They contain niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Wings supply iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as they contain minimal carbs.

items.title: Provides collagen
items.content: Skin and cartilage in wings are sources of collagen, beneficial for skin and joint health.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Even baked wings retain a notable amount of fat, especially when the skin is left on.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Excessive salt and sugary sauces can increase the risk of hypertension and add calories.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Contamination if undercooked
items.content: Insufficiently cooked wings may harbor pathogens such as Salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve wings hot, often with a dipping sauce. They are eaten by hand and can be paired with vegetable sticks, fries, or a salad. To reduce calories, choose skinless baked wings and light marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw wings refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Cooked baked wings can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
